Sure, here are the answers in 4–5 lines each:

**Q1. What are semiconductors?**  
Semiconductors are materials whose electrical conductivity lies between conductors and insulators. Examples include silicon and germanium. Their conductivity can be modified by adding impurities (doping) or changing temperature. They are the backbone of electronic devices like diodes and transistors.

**Q2. Why resistance of semiconductors decreases with increasing temperature?**  
As temperature increases, more electrons gain enough energy to jump from the valence band to the conduction band. This increases the number of charge carriers (electrons and holes), reducing resistance. Unlike metals, semiconductors become better conductors at higher temperatures.

**Q3. What is meant by forward and reverse biasing?**  
Forward biasing means connecting the positive terminal of a battery to the p-side and the negative to the n-side of a p-n junction, allowing current to flow. Reverse biasing is the opposite—positive to n-side and negative to p-side—preventing current flow. Biasing controls the operation of diodes.

In metals, resistance increases with temperature because atoms vibrate more as they get hotter. These vibrations cause more collisions between the free electrons (which carry current) and the atoms. More collisions mean electrons move less freely, increasing resistance. So, higher temperature → more atomic vibrations → higher resistance.
